title: Low-degree Fourier bound from switching failure
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f$ be a sign-valued Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube. Suppose $w$ is a positive integer and, for every nonnegative integer $d$, the probability that a random restriction with retention parameter $1/(20w)$ leaves decision-tree depth at least $d$ is at most $(1/4)^d$. Then for every nonnegative integer $k$, the sum of the absolute values of the Fourier coefficients of the real-valued version of $f$ over all coordinate subsets of size at most $k$ is at most $2(20w)^k$.
